en: Salutations to Him whose mind is absorbed in the supreme reality, who swiftly releases one from the bonds of worldly existence,
and who has revealed the supreme reality.
We offer our salutation forever to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 1 ||

We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśivendra, who was born from the lotus-hand of Paramaśivendra, who grants boons to those who bow before him, and whose feet have shaken off the mud of worldly defilement. || 2 ||
To him who was reclining upon a most exquisite bed on a lovely sandy bank within a bower-house by the Vijanā river;
We offer our salutation always to Sadāśivendra. || 3 ||
To the king of birds among those who have cast off desire, who possesses the divine jewels of tranquility and self-restraint,
and who is the subduer of the vast expanse of delusion.
We offer our prostration to Sadāśivendra. || 4 ||

We offer perpetual salutation to the Lord Sadāśiva-Indra, who bestows the knowledge of the Self upon those who take refuge in Him, who dwells at the pinnacle of the palace of the supreme reality of the Self, and whose intellect regards stone and gold as equal.

We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśiva, the Lord, who by means of awakening has destroyed the eightfold city [of the body] which was struck by the poison of swallowed ignorance, and who is the sun to the darkness of delusion.
We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśivendra, who bestows tranquility, the sixfold bliss, liberation, discernment, and dispassion, and who swiftly grants protection to those who bow before him.
We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśivendra, who has made the Kalpavallī of the Siddhānta his own work, who is devoted to Kapālin, and whose palm bears the fruit of liberation.
To him whose body was smeared with mud and grass, who viewed the world as lower even than a blade of grass,
and who wandered in the midst of the forest;
We offer our salutation always to Sadāśivendra. || 9 ||
To him who has captured the heart of Hari,
who has grasped the jewel of his own true nature,
and who is like the full moon to the ocean of those prostrate before him;
We offer our prostration to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 10 ||
To the one who is the full moon for the ocean of wisdom, which dispels the darkness of ignorance,
and who purifies the forest of sins through prostration;
We always offer our salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 11 ||

We offer salutations to Sadāśivendra, who is intent on bestowing the unity of the inner self with Brahman, who is skilled in removing the impurities of the mind, and whose heart is satisfied by mere remembrance [of Him]. 12.
To Sadāśivendra, whose pinnacle of realized wisdom was praised by his own guru Paramaśivendra, and whose heart is unwavering in the true reality— we offer our perpetual salutation. (13)
To him who, having dissolved the entire world, is devoted to the remaining indivisible reality,
and who eats food obtained from the mouth [of his guru].
We always offer salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 14 ||
To him who made his own arm a pillow,
who embraced dispassion as his garment, and who dwelt within the sky—
unto him [be salutation].
We offer our salutation always to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 15 ||

To Sadāśivendra, who is capable of revealing the essence of the entirety of all scriptures, whose side is bowed [in devotion], and whose nature is being, consciousness, and bliss— to him we offer perpetual salutation. 16.

We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśivendra, whose speech is skillful in instructing the vine-like disciples, who is the abode of abundant compassion, and who purifies the world with his very glance. 17.
To him in whose arm no modification arises even when it has been cut off and fallen by a barbarian, and who is unaware of the exertion of the notion of "mine"— to him [I bow].
We offer our prostration to Sadāśivendra. || 18 ||
To him, the bestower of siddhis, by whom flowers fell upon his head when the names of Ugra were uttered.
We always offer our salutation to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 19 ||
To this Lord Sadāśiva, the ocean of compassion, who by his power swiftly transforms even the worlds of the wicked into those preeminent with merit— to him we offer perpetual salutation. (20)
Salutations to Siddheśvara, who bestows purity upon the intellect, whose lotus feet are worshipped,
and who liberates those bound by the flood of worldly existence.
We offer our salutation always to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 21 ||
To the pair of feet of the one who pervades the world— feet that grant a succession of lotuses to those prostrate before them, even to those mute by birth— to that [pair of feet], [I bow].
We always offer our salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 22 ||
We always offer salutation to Sadāśivendra, who, by means of his loud proclamation, makes even those devoted to the tongue and the organ of generation detached from their own [sensual pleasures].
To the one who brings about desirable desires, who is skillful in removing fears that ought to be pacified,
and whose body resembles refined gold.
We always pay homage to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 24 ||
To the giver of the Tāraka-vidyā,
whose face dispels the pride of the Lord of the Stars (Śiva),
and who is intent upon the loud recitation [of the mantra].
We offer our prostration to Sadāśivendra. || 25 ||
If by his grace even a mute were to quickly attain world-transcending fame,
to this one of wondrous deeds—
We always pay homage to Sadāśivendra. || 26 ||
To him who is most distant from the wicked, easily accessible to the virtuous, whose hands are vessels [of merit],
and whose dwelling is at the foot of a tree.
We offer our prostration to Sadāśiva, the Lord. || 27 ||
To the one who ferries across the ocean of existence, who is devoted to Bhava, who is bowed down by those seeking his grace,
and who is free from the bonds of worldly existence.
We always offer our salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 28 ||
To him, who was as if performing the renunciation of his threefold body at the three sacred sites,
[the Lord] granted meditative absorption.
We always offer salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 29 ||
Because her compassion acts upon him— whether he be lustful with a conquered heart, cruel, peaceful, dull-witted, or wise.
We offer our prostration to Sadāśivendra. || 30 ||
To Sadāśivendra, who dispels the doubts of those who are uncertain regarding the characteristics and the objects characterized as found in the Vedas and Smṛtis, we offer perpetual salutation.
To him whose body resembles the dawn,
who has sportively shaken off the pride of desire, and who is restless within the supreme consciousness;
We always offer our salutation to Sadāśivendra. || 32 ||
We offer perpetual salutation to Sadāśivendra, who has been made our refuge by his excellent qualities, whose feet have been made into red lotuses, and who possesses a forbearance equal to the earth.
To the one who is bowed to by the most excellent ascetics and by Gaṇanātha, the remover of insurmountable obstacles;
to the Lord Sadāśiva, who has made the world his servant through his virtues—to him we offer perpetual salutation. 34.
To the one who forgives thousands of offenses committed by prostrate beings, the bestower of liberation through his very forbearance—
to that Lord Sadāśiva, we offer our perpetual salutation. (35)
We perpetually offer salutation to Śrī Dakṣiṇāmukha, the Lord Sadāśiva, who, having assumed a physical form, desires to bestow swift wisdom upon those who bow down to him.

With hearts afflicted by the threefold suffering, we— our greatness awakened by the most excellent Guru— constantly offer salutation to Sadāśivendra, who is skillful in removing the threefold suffering. 37.

O Lord, whose heart is ever dissolved in the Self, who knows the meaning of all the Vedas and Shastras, who delights in wandering along the banks of rivers, and who removes the distress from the hearts of all people;
O Master, whose lotus feet are sought by the world bowing down!
O Sadāśiva, O Yati, always bestow upon me your boundless compassion. || 38 ||

In the past, though his own hands were dripping with copious blood from the slaughter of Yavanas, he, overcome by compassion, led this man— a treasury of sins— who had bowed at his lotus feet, to a state free from falling.
May Sadāśiva, the ascetic, pour upon me boundless compassion. || 39 ||

O Sadāśiva, Lord of Ascetics and Sovereign of Great Yogis, upon the mind of one whose senses have been captivated by You, whose body has been struck down by diseases, and who is a dwelling place for manifold miseries, even the scent of tranquility and self-restraint vanishes; yet when such a person falls at Your feet, O Lord of Ascetics, quickly bestow upon me a compassion that is beyond all cause.

O Best among the powerful, O Lord, I am neither capable of composing hymns with collections of words fashioned by supreme ingenuity, nor do I possess the strength even for recitation and the like; therefore, O All-pervading One, grant me that which is free from causal motives.
O Sadāśiva, bestow your grace upon me, the foremost of yogis, quickly! 41.
Indeed, in this world, many people dwell at their pleasure, possessed of words, meanings,
and knowledge; but those possessed of ultimate realization have never before been seen or heard of.
Surely, O King of Ascetics, it is without you. || 42 ||
To him whose lotus-heart is pleased by even slight worship, who bears the form of the moon-crested Lord as his supreme manifestation,
and who swiftly removes the sorrow of those who bow before him.
Salutations to the Lord of Ascetics, for the ripening of merit. || 43 ||
I am not capable of conquering my senses,
nor am I able to perform worship, devotion, and the like;
protect me by Your very nature of compassion alone.
O Sadāśiva, ocean of compassion! || 44 ||

O Sadāśiva, supreme one who is eternally satisfied, quickly grant joy through this hymn of praise, which is performed with a head bowed at the tips of the rows of prostrations and possesses an exceedingly gentle awakening. 45.
Thus ends the *Śrīsadāśivendra-stava*, composed by the world-teacher of Śṛṅgeri, the venerable Śrī Śrī Saccidānandaśivābhinavanṛsiṃhabhāratī Mahāsvāmī.
